title: vidIQ Pricing 2026: Free, Boost and Max Plans
summary: vidIQ pricing features a free plan and three paid options for YouTube creators.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Those limits are the reason to check a few billing details before you pay for any tier.


Is vidIQ free to use? Yes, vidIQ has a free plan that you can use without paying, and it's enough to test whether the tool changes what you title, tag and publish.


Paid tiers lift limits on that free version. If you never hit one of those limits, you have no reason to upgrade yet.


### Can I cancel vidIQ or get a refund?


You can cancel a paid plan from your account settings, but refund terms are set by vidIQ's own policy and I won't paraphrase them from memory. Read the refund wording on vidIQ's billing and terms pages before you enter a card.


Cancelling normally stops the next charge and doesn't return the one already taken, so decide before the billing date, not after.


### Does vidIQ work for more than one channel?


It works with the YouTube channels you connect to your account, but how many a given plan covers is a plan-level limit, and it differs between tiers. If you run a main channel and a side channel, check that line on the pricing page first.


Cover only one channel and you pay twice or pick one, and that's a concrete limit worth paying to lift.


Is vidIQ worth it for a channel that isn't monetized yet? Usually not on a paid plan, because there's no revenue for the subscription to protect or grow.


Use the free plan, log the decisions it actually changed, and upgrade only when a specific cap slows a real upload. Once a channel earns money or publishes on a fixed schedule, the same cap costs you time you can price.


### Does vidIQ change its prices often?


Treat any figure in an article, this one included, as a snapshot, because plan names, bundles and prices have shifted over the years. The pricing page is the only source that is current on the day you buy.


Check it again at renewal, because a yearly plan renews at whatever the page says then, not at what you first saw.
